text:
rachel: throwing a wildcard: instead of swapping to a totally new list layout, what if we add column collapse toggles to the existing roles matrix? users can collapse rarely-used permission columns and surface only top-level actions. goal: keep the familiar grid but reduce noise for large orgs

noah: interesting. collapse state should be persisted per-org and maybe per-user? product question: do we want org-level defaults + personal overrides?

rachel: yes, default collapse config at org-level (admin can set a baseline), users can then pin their own view. also add a small CTA "Reset to org defaults" in the view menu.

tess: accessibility note: collapsing columns changes the table layout; screen readers should announce "column X hidden" and table summary should update. propose aria-live region to announce changes and include a control to restore columns for SR users.

ina: dev note: column collapse + virtualization is simpler than row virtualization changes, but we still need to recompute column widths and rerender cells. doable.

ux-bot: mock: https://figma.redwood/roles/col-collapse shows a little chevron at the column header + a menu with "Hide column" and keyboard hint: Shift+H to toggle. Also included a "Compact mode" toggle in the header that reduces paddings and turns permissions into icons with tooltips.

rachel: keyboard shortcuts idea: "/" focuses the role search, "g r" jumps to Roles, "?" opens the shortcuts help. we should surface an accessible shortcuts modal with a brief list and the ability to customize keymaps per user later.

noah: love it. ensure shortcuts are discoverable: a tiny "Keyboard shortcuts" link in the table header should open the modal. also provide a way to disable shortcuts for users who use screen readers (some SR users prefer to avoid global bindings).\
tess: SR specifics: when hiding columns we should maintain data parity for users relying on assistive tech. e.g., a collapsed "Compute" column that contained a key permission should not remove that permission from the accessible representation. Instead provide an aria-describedby summary on the role row that lists collapsed columns' top-level permissions. sample aria pattern: role=\"row\" aria-describedby=\"row-123-details\" and the details element contains a short list.

rachel: good point. we can show a condensed summary chip on each row like "+3 hidden perms" with aria-describedby linking to the hidden-perms content. hitting Enter on that chip expands a flyout with the list.

ina: audit integration thought: add an inline audit search preview in the header for quick filtering across the grid. like a small search field with syntax hints: "actor:anna action:invite resource:role". Hitting Enter opens the audit timeline in a right-side pane scoped to the current filters.

noah: product question: do we want role->audit deep link per-row? clicking the row's actions could open audit pre-filtered to that role. saves time for investigations.

rachel: yes. add a tiny "View audit" link in the row actions that opens the right pane with the role pre-filtered. also include a quick filter dropdown pre-populated with common filters (invites, permission-changes, SSO-changes).\
tess: for keyboard and SR: when the audit pane opens, it should trap focus, have role=dialog, aria-label=\"Audit timeline for <role>\", and have a clear keyboard shortcut to close (Esc). when closed, focus must return to the triggering control. use aria-live to say "Audit timeline opened for <role>" for VO users.

ina: performance note: audit pane should lazy-load the timeline and show a skeleton. also for the inline audit search in header, we should debounce and only prefetch suggestion hints, not results, until user confirms.

ux-bot: tooltip copy suggestions: for collapsed-column chip: "Some permissions are hidden from the table. Press Enter to view hidden permissions." for disabled SSO toggle (if we show it): "SSO enforcement is configured at the Organization level."

rachel: SSO UX callout: product only supports org-level SSO today. prefer showing a read-only "SSO: required" indicator in the org header and per-row show a passive badge "SSO enforced org-wide" only when org SSO is on. avoid disabled toggles inside rows to reduce confusion.

tess: agree. additionally voiceover-specific tip: on macOS VoiceOver, long aria-labels may get truncated. build a concise summary first (role name + members) and provide a separate region with expanded details that VoiceOver users can open. example summary aria: "Billing Admin, 4 members" and expanded region text: "Can create API keys, view invoices, manage billing settings"

noah: small UX nit: when multiple columns are collapsed we should show a multi-collapse chip like "3 columns hidden" and allow a modal to manage columns with checkboxes for visibility. this improves discoverability vs hunting headers.

rachel: good. action items: nina: prototype header inline audit search + right-pane lazy-load behavior. tess: write accessible patterns for column collapse, collapsed-perms summary, audit pane SR announcements, and keyboard-shortcuts modal. noah: implement keyboard registry and disable-for-SR preference. ux-bot: update figma with collapse chips, audit search mock, shortcuts modal, and SSO badge variations. meet Thursday 4pm for review.

rachel: added to calendar. tagging @here for folks who want to join :bell:
